es.summary: El ácido acetilsalicílico (AAS) inhibe irreversiblemente la ciclooxigenasa, reduciendo la síntesis de tromboxano A2 y la agregación plaquetaria.
key_points: Inhibición irreversible de la COX‑1 en plaquetas
Usado para prevención primaria y secundaria de eventos cardiovasculares
Aumenta el riesgo de úlcera gástrica y sangrado gastrointestinal
Se suspende 7‑10 días antes de cirugías mayores
No se recomienda en pacientes con alergia a salicilatos

mechanism: Bloquea la enzima COX‑1 en plaquetas, impidiendo la formación de tromboxano A2
Disminuye la activación y agregación plaquetaria de forma irreversible
Efecto persiste durante la vida de la plaqueta (≈7‑10 días)
indications: Prevención secundaria de infarto agudo de miocardio y accidente cerebrovascular isquémico
Profilaxis de trombosis en pacientes con enfermedad arterial coronaria
Manejo del dolor leve‑moderado y fiebre (uso secundario)
contraindications: Hipertensión gastrointestinal activa o úlcera péptica
interactions: Aumenta el riesgo de sangrado con anticoagulantes (warfarina, heparina)
Potencia el efecto de otros AAS y NSAIDs
Reduce la eficacia de antihipertensivos como los inhibidores de la ECA
Puede interferir con metotrexato, aumentando su toxicidad
nursing_care: Verificar ausencia de úlcera gástrica activa antes de administrar
Controlar signos de sangrado: hematuria, melena, hematomas
Observar presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca después de dosis inicial
Retener la dosis si el paciente presenta hemorragia activa y notificar al médico
Documentar hora de la última dosis antes de procedimientos quirúrgicos
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento con alimentos o antiácidos para minimizar irritación gástrica
Reportar cualquier sangrado inusual, como encías sangrantes o sangre en heces
Evitar el consumo simultáneo de alcohol y otros antiinflamatorios
Informar al equipo de salud antes de cirugías o procedimientos dentales
antidote_overdose: Lavado gástrico si la ingestión es reciente
Alcalinización con bicarbonato de sodio IV para acelerar la excreción
Monitoreo de gases arteriales y función renal

outcomes: Sin evidencia de sangrado activo durante la hospitalización

interventions.action: Evaluar historial de úlceras y uso de anticoagulantes antes de iniciar AAS
interventions.rationale: Identificar factores que aumentan el riesgo de hemorragia

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y nivel de hemoglobina cada 12 h
Inspeccionar mucosas, piel y orina en busca de sangrado oculto
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si aparecen hemorragias gastrointestinales o epistaxis persistente
Educar al paciente sobre signos de sangrado y cuándo buscar ayuda

en.summary: Acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase, reducing thromboxane A2 synthesis and platelet aggregation.
key_points: Used for primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events
Increases risk of gastric ulcer and gastrointestinal bleeding
Not recommended for patients with salicylate allergy

mechanism: Blocks COX‑1 enzyme in platelets, preventing thromboxane A2 formation
Irreversibly decreases platelet activation and aggregation
Effect persists for the life of the platelet (≈7‑10 days)
indications: Secondary prevention of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and ischemic stroke (IS)
Prophylaxis of thrombosis in patients with coronary artery disease
Management of mild‑moderate pain and fever (secondary use)
contraindications: Active gastrointestinal hypertension or peptic ulcer
interactions: Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin)
Potentiates effects of other ASA and NSAIDs
Reduces efficacy of antihypertensives such as ACE inhibitors
May interfere with methotrexate, increasing toxicity
nursing_care: Verify absence of active gastric ulcer before administration
Monitor for signs of bleeding: hematuria, melena, bruising
Observe blood pressure and heart rate after initial dose
Withhold dose if patient has active hemorrhage and notify provider
Document time of last dose before surgical procedures
patient_teaching: Take medication with food or antacids to minimize gastric irritation
Report any unusual bleeding, such as bleeding gums or blood in stool
Avoid simultaneous alcohol and other anti‑inflammatories
Inform healthcare team before surgeries or dental procedures
antidote_overdose: Gastric lavage if ingestion is recent
Alkalinization with IV sodium bicarbonate to accelerate excretion
Monitor arterial gases and renal function

outcomes: No evidence of active bleeding during hospitalization

interventions.action: Assess ulcer history and anticoagulant use before initiating ASA
interventions.rationale: Identify factors that increase hemorrhage risk

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and hemoglobin every 12 h
Inspect mucous membranes, skin, and urine for hidden bleeding
Withhold dose and notify provider if gastrointestinal bleeding or persistent epistaxis occurs
Educate patient on bleeding signs and when to seek help

key_points.1.quote: Some of those indications are secondary prevention of stroke, coronary artery disease, acute coronary syndromes, primary prevention of cardiovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, and prevention of thromboembolism in clients with certain heart valves.

key_points.2.quote: However, in addition to the effect on platelets, aspirin can also increase the risk of gastric ulcer formation through inhibition of gastric prostaglandin synthesis.

sections.indications.1.quote: Some of those indications are secondary prevention of stroke, coronary artery disease, acute coronary syndromes, primary prevention of cardiovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, and prevention of thromboembolism in clients with certain heart valves.

sections.indications.2.quote: It also has anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, which allow it to be used for pain, inflammatory conditions, and fever.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: A history of bleeding complications, such as intracranial hemorrhage or gastrointestinal bleeding, may be considered a contraindication to further antiplatelet therapy, depending on the circumstances and the drug.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: An immune-mediated side effect caused by exposure to heparin products is known as heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) .

sections.interactions.0.quote: HIT can be managed effectively by immediately stopping all forms of heparin therapy and other anticoagulant agents like direct thrombin inhibitors (e.g., argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux) to avoid further thrombosis.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: It should be avoided in clients with active pathological bleeding or a history of intracranial hemorrhage.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Some symptoms of bleeding are blood in the stool; dark, tarry-appearing stools; blood in the urine; epistaxis; gingival bleeding; very severe headache; coffee-ground emesis; and hemoptysis.
